text: Last lesson turned a frustrated complaint into a specific requirement: one tested customer table, sourced from raw_customers, with a guaranteed unique, non-null customer ID. This lesson turns that requirement into a concrete plan for the dbt project — before we open dbt or write a single line of SQL.

Every well-built dbt project, including this tiny one, follows the same three-layer pattern. Sources: a YAML declaration pointing at raw data that's already sitting in the warehouse — not something dbt builds, just a pointer. Staging: one model per source table, doing light cleanup only — renaming columns, casting types, nothing else. And marts: the final, reportable tables, where real business logic and joins actually belong. Skipping this plan is how beginners end up with one giant model trying to do everything at once, which is painful to debug and impossible to reuse.

For this project, that pattern gets about as small as it can get while still being real. One source: raw_customers, already loaded in Snowflake. One staging model: stg_jaffle_shop__customers, following the standard naming convention. And one mart model: customers, the final table finance and support will actually query. Two real models, total. That's the whole project.

Order matters here, and it's not arbitrary. The mart model you'll write in Lesson 8 references the staging model with a ref() call — ref('stg_jaffle_shop__customers') — and that only resolves once the staging model actually exists. So this project has to be built bottom-up: declare the source first, build staging next, then build the mart on top. Planning the layers now is what makes that build order obvious later, instead of something you discover by hitting an error.

And just as important: this plan has no intermediate layer. In bigger projects, an intermediate layer exists to join multiple staging models before a final mart — but with only one source table here, there's nothing yet to join. A correct, minimal project beats an over-engineered one for a first real build.

That's the plan: source, staging model, mart model, in that order. Next lesson, we get the raw data itself into Snowflake — real CREATE STAGE and COPY INTO syntax, loading raw_customers.csv before dbt ever touches it.
